# notify

> Self-hosted Web Push notifications over HTTP, CLI, and MCP. One Bun process, one SQLite database.

## Agent contract

- Server: `{BASE_URL}`
- Agent contract: `GET {BASE_URL}/llms.txt`
- Machine-readable setup: `notify setup --json`

## MCP

- Endpoint: `POST {BASE_URL}/mcp`
- Transport: Streamable HTTP, stateless
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer ntk_...`
- Discovery: call `tools/list`; tool names, descriptions, and JSON input schemas are returned by the server.
- Use a send-only token (`notify:send`) unless administration is required.

Tools:

- `notify` — `{ channel?, title?, body, url?, tag?, data? }`. Omit `channel` for the default channel.
- `list_channels` — visible channels.
- `list_devices` — devices with subscription IDs; push endpoints are never returned.
- `list_notifications` — recent notifications.
- `create_channel` — admin-gated, `channels:write`.
- `register_device` — admin-gated, `devices:write`; returns a one-time enrollment URL, terminal QR, and optional `ttlMs`.
- `manage_subscription` — admin-gated, `devices:write`; takes a subscription ID and `delete`/`disable`.

Admin tools are not registered unless `MCP_ADMIN_ENABLED=1`, and still require the right scope.

## CLI

```bash
notify setup --json
notify send "message" --channel <slug> --json
notify register --channel <slug> --ttl 24h --json
notify notifications list --json
notify notifications show <id> --json
notify subscription list --json
notify token create --name agent --scope notify:send --json
```

## Storage

`notifications` stores every send, including sends with no subscriptions. `deliveries` stores one row per subscription attempt with status, HTTP status code, and error. `RETENTION_DAYS` prunes old rows.
